Ah, excellent example in the context of the article.

Doing a simple black box analysis of the brain, we see that some information goes in through senses and different information comes out through actuators. Thus, information has been processed.

This article is hot garbage. Of course the brain doesn't function on the exact same methods as a fucking computer, but the analogy is still valid.

We absorb stimuli from the world, it is converted into meaningful information by the cortexes in our brain, and is then processed by the different areas of our brain responsible for conscious and unconscious thought. How is that any different than a computer taking bits of data, converting them to useful formats, and then using its multiple components to interpret that data? Without a brain capable of converting and processing data, sounds and smells and sights would just be incomprehensible messes that we can't do anything with. Just because we aren't physically storing memories or knowledge in the form of static cells in our brain that we physically access to remember things, doesn't make the computer analogy completely invalid. We are still "processing" data from the world around us, the only difference being that our brain isn't compartmentalized like a computer. We process information with the same parts of our brain we use to "store" it. Just because you can't find a memory with a microscope, doesn't mean it doesn't exist on any physical level. Where does the author think memories come from? Does she think we're just pulling them out of the ether every time we remember something? We're not. They're in your brain. They might not be there in complete form or in any form that we could ever hope to perceive on a physical level, but to say they aren't there makes just as little sense as saying they're there in a static form.

I understand the point of the article. The computer analogy is a bit flawed and doesn't fully represent the human mind, but it's not nearly as flawed as the author is trying to make it. The human brain is very much comparable to a computer even if there are some significant differences.

**Daily Devotional**

**May 20**

*11 My son, despise not the chastening of the LORD; neither be weary of his correction:12 For whom the LORD loveth he correcteth; even as a father the son in whom he delighteth. (Proverbs 3:11-12 KJV)*

This verse was in the Old Testament, but was quoted in the New Testament (Hebrews 12:5-6), and is something that all the children of God should expect from their Heavenly Father. It needs to be noted that when the Lord chastens us, it is always corrective, and is not like some pastors teach, that God puts sickness on us. Would any human father do that? In this church age, God never punishes us, as He put His entire wrath upon Jesus, who bore it all for us. The way God corrects us is through His Word, and not His wrath (2 Timothy 3:16).

Many people have been taught that all kinds of sickness, diseases, trials and tribulations come from God to teach us something, but it is just not true (James 1:13). Jesus was the exact image of the Father, and He never put sickness or harm on anyone, so that shows that God does not either. God is a good God, and all things that are good and perfect come from Him (James 1:17), and all the bad things come from the devil (John 10:10). If you attribute the actions of the devil to be from God, it is the blasphemy of the Holy Ghost that Jesus said was unforgivable (Matthew 12:31-32), and can send even a born again Christian to hell. See our web page “New Revelations” for more information on this. Our God is so good; don’t blame Him for the works of the devil.

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com
